observations:
Torah #150 is the shortest teaching examined in this dataset — 2 lines, 0 bechina edges in torahData.js, 3 proposed concept nodes. The threshold for a new package is 3+ bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain. That threshold is technically met (3 nodes are proposed), but all three nodes belong to the same unified domain — the miraculous hidden protection enabling Yosef's trial — and they form one inseparable thematic cluster, not independent domains.

The sole package identified (Package 1: דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקֶן וְנִסָּיוֹן הַנִּסְתָּר) is the only possible grouping for the entire content of this Torah. There is no second domain.

Specifically, no new independent domain emerges because:

1. No evil mirror domain: The teaching does not name, describe, or develop any evil-side concept. The temptation (yetzer hara, the wife of Potiphar, the force of sin) is not mentioned or analyzed — it is only implicit as the background of the trial. Without any named evil concepts, no evil package can form. This Torah is a rare example of a teaching that does not develop its evil mirror at all.

2. No epistemological domain: Torah #150 does not introduce a wisdom/sekhel/da'at cluster. The phrase 'אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ' (does not know) might superficially suggest a knowledge/ignorance axis, but the teaching does not develop this into a cluster of concepts. The not-knowing is a consequence of hiddenness, not a distinct thematic domain.

3. No ritual/prayer/Torah domain: The teaching makes no reference to mitzvot, prayer, Torah study, or any ritual practice. It is purely aggadic-reflective in nature.

4. No sefirotic or cosmic structure: Unlike most Rebbe Nachman teachings of this length, Torah #150 does not map its concepts onto kabbalistic structures (sefirot, partzufim, divine names, Hebrew letters). It is a plain reflection in the language of wonder and hiddenness.

5. No ancestral/lineage domain separate from the image domain: While the concept of the father's image (דמות דיוקנו של אביו) implies a broader domain of ancestral merit and zechut avot, the teaching does not develop this axis. Yaakov is mentioned only as the source of the image, not as a concept being identified with anything else. A lineage/protection domain would require at least one more named concept explicitly connected to it in the text — which is absent.

Conclusion: Torah #150 yields exactly 1 package (good polarity), 3 proposed bechina-candidate nodes, and 0 new independent packages beyond what is captured in torah_150_packages.json. The teaching's extreme brevity and meditative (rather than structural) nature means that no multi-domain architecture is present or needed.
